alias-of:antipatris_70>aphek_72@a0c9e4.note: Text names only Antipatris (23.31), not Aphek. Identifying the two comes from outside sources.

alias-of:azotus_132>ashdod_101@3f9e6b.note: Text names only Azotus (8.40), not Ashdod. The identification comes from outside sources.

alias-of:ptolemais_959>acco_15@da70ef.note: Text names only Ptolemais (21.7), not Acco. The identification comes from outside sources.

date:first-missionary-journey@477e44.note: Text gives no year. Sent out by the Holy Ghost from Antioch (13.2-4). The year 45-46 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:peter-defends-gentile-salvation@a2f.note: Text gives no year. Peter's defence at Jerusalem (11.2-18). The year 38 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:peter-heals-aeneas-and-dorcas@a2f1a.note: Text gives no year. Aeneas healed at Lydda (9.33-35), Dorcas raised at Joppa (9.40). The year 38 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:peter-meets-cornelius@a2f1a4.note: Text gives no year. Cornelius's vision (10.1-8), then Peter arrives at Caesarea (10.24). The year 38 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:peter-preaches-to-gentiles-in-caesa.note: Text gives no year. Peter preaches to Cornelius's household at Caesarea (10.24-44). The year 38 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:saul-is-converted@66b37a.note: Text gives no year. Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus, then baptism (9.3-18). The year 32 depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:saul-proclaims-jesus@a2f1a4.note: Text gives no year. He preaches at Damascus at once (9.20), 'after many days' (9.23). The year 38 depends on dating outside Scripture.

near:akeldama_43>jerusalem_636@b86894.note: Text says the field was known to the dwellers at Jerusalem and called Aceldama (1.19). Nearness is not stated; the distance comes from outside sources.

occurred-at:journey-to-rome-begins>adram.note: 27.2 names Adramyttium only as the home port of the ship boarded. No departure port is named; the next stop was Sidon (27.3).

occurred-at:journey-to-rome-begins>alexa.note: They found the Alexandrian ship at Myra (27.5-6); Alexandria is only the ship's home port. The journey did not start there.

occurred-at:journey-to-rome-begins>asia_.note: 27.2 says only that they meant to sail by the coasts of Asia. The first stop was Sidon (27.3), so Asia is a route, not the start.

occurred-at:paul-s-journey-to-rome>adram.note: 27.2 names Adramyttium only as the home port of the ship boarded. No departure port is named; the next stop was Sidon (27.3).

occurred-at:paul-s-journey-to-rome>alexa.note: They found the Alexandrian ship at Myra (27.5-6); Alexandria is only the ship's home port. The journey did not start there.

occurred-at:paul-s-journey-to-rome>syrti.note: Syrtis is not named. 27.17 speaks of 'the quicksands', and identifying them with Syrtis comes from outside sources.

part-of:seleucia_1045>aram_82@027378.note: Text names Seleucia (13.4) and Syria (15.41), not that Seleucia lies in Aram. The port's location and the Aram-Syria identity come from outside sources.

participated-in:agabus_107>disciples-fir.note: 11.26 names the disciples called Christians at Antioch without Agabus. He appears only afterward, with his prophecy (11.27-28).

participated-in:agabus_107>third-mission.note: Agabus prophesies at Caesarea near the end of the trip (21.10-11). The text does not name the journey; its span comes from outside chronology.

participated-in:alexander_187>peter-and-.note: 4.6 names an Alexander among the high priest's family at the council. It does not say he is Simon's son, so this is probably a different man.

participated-in:alphaeus_192>matthias-re.note: 1.13 names James the son of Alphaeus among the eleven, not Alphaeus. Alphaeus is named only as James's father.

participated-in:augustus_366>agrippa-and.note: Augustus is not at the hearing. 25.21 names him only as the court to which Paul appealed, so Festus keeps Paul until he can send him.

participated-in:augustus_366>paul-goes-b.note: Augustus is not in the hearing before Agrippa (25.23). 25.25 says only that Paul appealed to him.

participated-in:candace_916>conversion-o.note: 8.27 names Candace only as the queen the eunuch served. The eunuch is the one who believes and is baptized (8.37-38).

participated-in:demas_1006>paul-s-first-.note: Demas is with Paul as a fellow-worker sending greetings (Phlm 1.24; Col 4.14), while Paul is a prisoner (Phlm 1.9). Identifying that imprisonment with Acts 28 is outside.

participated-in:epaphras_1195>paul-s-fir.note: Phlm 1.23 calls Epaphras Paul's fellowprisoner. Identifying that imprisonment as Paul's first Roman one, as in Acts 28, comes from outside sources.

participated-in:holy_spirit_7400>saul-pr.note: 9.17 says Saul would be filled with the Holy Ghost before he preached (9.20). The Spirit is not named as acting in the preaching itself.

participated-in:james_719>an-angel-rescu.note: 12.17 names James only as the one Peter tells afterward; James is not present at the rescue. Whether he is the Lord's brother is outside identification.

participated-in:james_719>second-mission.note: James acts only at the Jerusalem council (15.13), before the journey begins (15.36-40). He is not named in the journey.

participated-in:jesus_905>the-holy-spiri.note: Jesus speaks of the promise of the Father and says they shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost (1.4-5).

participated-in:luke_1836>paul-casts-dem.note: 16.16 has 'we' with Paul, who is named (16.10). Luke is not named in Acts; identifying the narrator's 'we' as Luke comes from outside.

participated-in:luke_1836>paul-s-first-r.note: 28.16 says 'we came to Rome', with Paul. Col 4.14 names Luke with Paul. Identifying the narrator as Luke and the imprisonment as Acts 28's is outside.

participated-in:peter_2745>second-missio.note: Peter speaks at the Jerusalem council (15.7), before the journey begins (15.36-40). He is not named in the journey.

participated-in:philip_2347>third-missio.note: Paul's company lodges with Philip at Caesarea (21.8), near the journey's end. The text does not name the journey; its span comes from outside chronology.

participated-in:silas_2740>call-to-maced.note: Silas goes with Paul from 15.40, but is not named in the vision scene (16.9-10). Placing him in the 'we' company there is an inference.

participated-in:silas_2740>lydia-s-conve.note: Silas is with Paul from 15.40 and named with him at Philippi (16.19). He is not named in 16.13-15; this is an inference.

participated-in:silas_2740>timothy-joins.note: Silas is with Paul from 15.40, but 16.1-3 names only Paul and Timotheus in the joining. His presence is an inference.

participated-in:simon_2753>peter-meets-c.note: Simon the tanner is Peter's host at Joppa (10.6, 10.32). The Joppa brethren who went with Peter (10.23) are not named as including him.

participated-in:timotheus_2863>call-to-m.note: Timotheus joins Paul at Lystra (16.1-3) and travels with the company. He is not named in the vision scene (16.9-10); this is an inference.

participated-in:timotheus_2863>lydia-s-c.note: Timotheus travels with Paul from Lystra (16.3-4). He is not named at Philippi (16.13-15); this is an inference from the company.

participated-in:timotheus_2863>paul-cast.note: Timotheus travels with Paul from Lystra (16.3-4). He is not named in 16.16-18; this is an inference from the company.

participated-in:trophimus_2880>paul-arre.note: 21.29 says the Jews had seen Trophimus with Paul in the city and supposed Paul brought him into the temple. He is not shown in the arrest.

visited:aeneas_106>joppa_652@19eacb.note: 9.33 places Aeneas at Lydda, where Peter healed him. Joppa is where Dorcas lived (9.36), not Aeneas.

visited:alexander_187>jerusalem_636@67d0.note: 4.6 places an Alexander among the high priest's family at Jerusalem. It does not say he is Simon's son; probably a different man.

visited:aristarchus_306>syrtis_1123@3fcb.note: Aristarchus sails with Paul (27.2). Syrtis is not named; 'the quicksands' (27.17) is identified with it from outside sources.

visited:cornelius_956>joppa_652@1b2cff.note: Cornelius is at Caesarea (10.1, 10.24). He sends men to Joppa (10.5-8) instead of going there himself.

visited:dorcas_2810>lydda_741@0d3243.note: 9.36 places Dorcas at Joppa, where she died. The disciples there send to Lydda for Peter (9.38).

visited:elymas_403>salamis_1016@4e722b.note: 13.6-8 places Elymas at Paphos, opposing Paul before the deputy. Salamis is where they preached in the synagogues (13.5).

visited:elymas_403>seleucia_1045@c52690.note: Elymas is at Paphos (13.6-8). Seleucia is only where Paul's company departed from (13.4).

visited:julius_1763>syrtis_1123@593d03.note: Julius the centurion is aboard the ship (27.11). Syrtis is not named; 'the quicksands' (27.17) is identified with it from outside sources.

visited:paul_2479>syrtis_1123@bff38a.note: Paul sails on the ship (27.2). Syrtis is not named; 'the quicksands' (27.17) is identified with it from outside sources.

visited:paul_2479>tyre_1184@656936.note: They landed at Tyre and tarried seven days with the disciples (21.3-4), Paul among them.

visited:sceva_2480>ephesus_400@98b05a.note: The seven sons of Sceva act at Ephesus (19.14, 19.17). The text names the father but does not place him there.

visited:sergius_2502>seleucia_1045@1d75f.note: Sergius Paulus is the deputy at Paphos (13.7). Seleucia is only where Paul's company departed from (13.4).

visited:simon_2753>saron_1063@fc0ea3.note: Simon the tanner lodges at Joppa, by the sea (9.43, 10.6), not at Sharon.
